record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: When one or both sides of a Stable Marriage with Ties and Incomplete lists instance are derived from master lists, can those structural constraints be exploited to obtain better approximation guarantees for maximum-cardinality stable matching?

evidence.quote: it is an open question as to whether improved upper bounds exist in the presence of master lists on one or both sides.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An instance of the Stable Marriage problem with Ties and Incomplete lists (SMTI) consists of a set U of men and a set W of women. Each person p has a preference list that ranks an acceptable subset of the opposite side; the ranking is a weak order, i.e., it may contain ties (groups of equally preferred partners). Acceptability is symmetric: w appears on m's list if and only if m appears on w's list.

A matching M is a set of mutually acceptable pairs in which each person appears in at most one pair. A pair (m,w) not in M is a blocking pair (in the weak stability sense) if m and w find each other acceptable, and each of m,w is either unmatched in M or strictly prefers the other to their current partner in M. A matching is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. The MAX-SMTI problem asks for a weakly stable matching of maximum cardinality.

A master list for one side is a single weak order over all members of that side such that every preference list on the other side is the restriction of this master list to the acceptable partners. The instance is said to be derived from master lists on one (resp. both) sides if such a master list exists on that side (resp. on both sides).

It is known that MAX-SMTI is NP-hard and admits a polynomial-time 3/2-approximation algorithm in the general case, while no approximation ratio below 4/3 (and not below some smaller explicit constant such as roughly 21/19) is achievable under standard complexity assumptions.

Question: When the preferences on one side, or on both sides, are derived from a master list, does there exist a polynomial-time approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI with approximation ratio strictly better than 3/2? More generally, determine the best possible polynomial-time approximation ratio for MAX-SMTI restricted to instances with a master list on one side, and restricted to instances with master lists on both sides.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the general 3/2-approximation for MAX-SMTI (Király) and hardness lower bounds (≈1.1052 unconditionally, 4/3 under UGC), as well as polynomial-time solvability of certain master-list variants of stable roommates, but did not surface any improved approximation algorithm for MAX-SMTI specifically exploiting one-sided or two-sided master lists. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hardness and Approximation Results for Some Variants of Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation and hardness results for SMTI variants; lower bounds around 1.1052 unless P=NP and 1.25 under UGC.
status_evidence.claim: Best known general MAX-SMTI ratio remains 3/2 with hardness bounds well below it, and improvements for master-list-restricted instances are not reported.

status_evidence.title: Stable Marriage with Incomplete Lists and Ties (Iwama–Manlove)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational NP-hardness and approximation results for MAX-SMTI.
status_evidence.claim: General MAX-SMTI is NP-hard; no specialized improved bound for master-list instances is cited.
